page: Microsoft Azure D64lds_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the Dldsv6 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, featuring 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. This instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It also includes 3780 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64lds_v6 demonstrates strong compute and memory performance. The instance achieves a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 20508.0 and a strong Passmark CPU score of 70905.37. Memory performance is highlighted by a strong read-only large block bandwidth of 254.01 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 109.18 GB/sec. The system also excels in data processing tasks, delivering a top-tier static web serving throughput of 97.56 GB/sec and a strong Redis SET performance of 83.04 million operations per second. For machine learning workloads, it processes 70B parameter LLM prompts at a top-tier rate of 39.92 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D64lds_v6 offers a high density of compute resources and substantial local storage capacity, making it a viable option for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. However, the low memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive databases or large-scale in-memory analytics. This instance is best suited for workloads such as high-throughput web serving, software compilation, image processing, and moderate-scale database operations that benefit from fast local storage and high-frequency CPU cores.
